items.title: Mayoral election volunteer stabbed while putting up signs in Mississauga
items.summary: A Mississauga mayoral candidate says police are investigating after a volunteer with his campaign was attacked and stabbed Monday night while putting up election signs. The volunteer was installing signs in the Park Royal area on behalf of City of Mississauga Ward 2 Coun. ” Peel Regional Police didn’t immediately provide any details about the incident, telling INSAUGA Canada they are still gathering information. The Tedjo campaign didn’t provide any additional details about the incident or victim beyond the candidate’s statement. “Last night, one of our volunteers was confronted by a stranger and attacked with a knife while installing election signs. Thankfully, our volunteer only suffered non-life-threatening injuries,” Tedjo’s statement reads. “I have spoken with the victim to offer my support as they recover from this altercation. I have also been in touch with Peel Police as they investigate this incident. “Our campaign has always been about bringing positive change to Mississauga and building a safer city,” the statement continues. “Most importantly, our campaign is run on the strength of volunteers who generously donate their time because they believe in a better Mississauga. ” Subscribe now to receive our daily email of today’s top stories in your city!

items.title: Retail theft charges in Mississauga and Brampton on pace to soar past 2025 total
items.summary: Retail theft charges in Mississauga and Brampton are already matching the total from all of last year, with police warning that organized networks are increasingly behind the crimes. Peel Regional Police laid 2,241 retail theft-related charges in the first eight months of 2026, just 69 fewer than the 2,310 charges laid during all of 2025. Deputy Chief Marc Andrews revealed the figures Tuesday (Oct. 6) as Peel Police hosted a two-day conference in Mississauga focused on organized retail crime. With four months still remaining in the year, the current pace puts Peel on track to significantly surpass last year’s total. If charges continue at roughly the same rate through the end of the year, the total could reach more than 3,300. But Andrews said the numbers represent more than a rise in isolated shoplifting incidents. “What we have seen across Peel and across Ontario is something far more coordinated, sophisticated, sinister and far-reaching,” he said. Andrews said police are finding that crimes initially believed to be unrelated are often connected to the same repeat offenders and criminal networks. “What looked like individual crimes were often part of a larger organized operation extending beyond a single community or jurisdiction,” he said.

items.title: Early voting for mayor and other posts now open in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga residents can vote early in the upcoming municipal election starting today. The City of Mississauga says people don’t have to wait until election day, Oct. 26, to choose their preferred candidates in the races for mayor, 11 city council seats and trustee positions at both school boards. Eligible voters in Mississauga can cast their ballots in advance at any number of locations across the city between Oct. 6 and Oct. 11. They can do so at Mississauga City Hall on Oct. 6-7 and at various other places from Oct. 8-11. “Advance voting gives voters more days and more locations to cast their ballot before election day,” the city said, adding it’s the same voting process, just offered earlier to allow voters to choose a time that works best for them. “Advance voting helps make voting easier, reduces lineups and gives voters more flexibility. If you have work, school, caregiving responsibilities, travel plans or other commitments on Oct. ” For those who wait until election day to cast their ballots, they must do so at a voting location in the Mississauga ward in which they live or own property, according to the city. Those voting in the upcoming election must bring along their voter notification card, if they’ve received one, and one piece of acceptable identification, city officials said.

items.title: NO SCHOOL: Peel Region students in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon have 3-day Thanksgiving weekend
items.summary: Students in the Peel District School Board and Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board will be off Monday, Oct. 12 for the Thanksgiving holiday and Monday, Oct. 26 for a PA day. The Peel District School Board and Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board have similar calendars for 2026-27. Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon students at both the Peel District School Board and Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board will enjoy a three-day Thanksgiving weekend thanks to a statutory holiday on Monday, Oct. 12. While some Ontario school boards have extended the holiday weekend with a Professional Activity (PA) day on the Friday prior to Thanksgiving, that’s not the case for students in the Peel District School Board and the Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board. Their next PA day is scheduled for Monday, Oct. 26. Here are all the key dates families need for the 2026-27 school year — PA days, March break, exam schedules and local things to do over the long weekend. Regular school year calendars for both boards indicate the next PA day is Monday, Oct. 26 for elementary and secondary students.

items.title: Mississauga Road Reopens After Overnight Crash Leaves One Driver in Critical Condition
items.summary: According to Insauga, one driver was left in critical condition after a two-vehicle crash on Mississauga Road near Featherston Drive on Monday night. Peel Regional Police said both drivers were injured and taken to a local trauma centre following the collision. The crash happened at the intersection with Featherston Drive, prompting police to close Mississauga Road between Burnhamthorpe Road West and Harkiss Road. Insauga reports the road has since reopened to traffic. Police have not released further details on what caused the collision.

items.title: Tedjo Jabs at Empty Podium as Parrish Skips Latest Mississauga Mayoral Debate
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, three of Mississauga's four leading mayoral candidates faced off in a debate Monday night hosted by Policorner at City Hall, with an empty podium left for Mayor Carolyn Parrish, who chose not to attend. Bonnie Crombie, Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla took questions on stage, and Tedjo opened the debate by joking that he had seen Parrish's car in the parking lot, comparing her absence to skipping a job interview for a position she's reapplying for. The Star reports Parrish has said she committed to only three debates this campaign and prefers smaller, in-person formats like backyard groups, school gyms and church auditoriums over formal debate stages. Parrish told the Star last week that debates turn into a wrestling match verbally and don't leave enough time to properly explain her positions. She posted a video of herself speaking at a church gathering Monday night instead of attending the debate.

items.title: Incumbent Faces Office-Administration Challenger for Dufferin-Peel Catholic Board's Ward 7 Trustee Seat
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, an incumbent trustee and challenger Diana Carlesimo are the two candidates running for Mississauga's Ward 7 seat on the Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board in the Oct. 26 municipal election. Carlesimo, who works in office administration, told the outlet she has lived in Ward 7 her entire life after growing up and going to school there. She said her grandparents immigrated to Mississauga from Italy in the 1950s and 1960s, and that every generation of her family has lived in the city since. Carlesimo said she has no political experience, but has volunteered at her children's school and on committees at the school board level. The Ward 7 trustee race is one of several Dufferin-Peel Catholic board contests appearing on Mississauga ballots alongside the mayoral and city council races this fall.

items.title: Voters in Toronto and Mississauga Can Begin Casting Advance Ballots as Both Mayoral Races Tighten
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, voters in both Toronto and Mississauga can begin casting ballots in advance of this month's municipal election as of Tuesday. Residents don't need photo identification to vote, but must bring a piece of ID showing their name and a Toronto or Mississauga address, depending on where they're voting. Any eligible voter can cast a ballot at any of the advance voting locations in their city, rather than being restricted to a single assigned site. CityNews reports both mayoral races are widely expected to go down to the wire. In Mississauga, incumbent Carolyn Parrish faces challenges from former mayor Bonnie Crombie and councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla. In Toronto, incumbent Olivia Chow is being challenged by Councillor Brad Bradford and former MP Chris Alexander.

items.title: Poll Finds Mississauga Voters Reject Personal Attacks in Mayoral Race, Even as Debate Clips Go Viral Online
items.summary: According to a Liaison Strategies poll reported by the Toronto Star, most Mississauga residents describe the mayoral campaign as mostly mean-spirited or a mix of respectful and mean-spirited following a heated debate last week. Three-quarters of those surveyed said personal comments or insults have no place in an election campaign, while just under a third said the race has been mostly personal attacks rather than policy debate. About 30 per cent described a mixture of personal and policy exchanges, and 17 per cent called it mostly fair political debate. The poll was conducted in the two days after the debate, which has since been widely shared online in short clips. Liaison Strategies principal David Valentin told the Star that fewer people are watching full debates but still catching the viral snippets that circulate afterward. Valentin added that voters routinely say they dislike negative campaigning even though, by his account, nothing proves more effective than negative ads.

items.title: Boy recounts 1994 park attack on tape played at trial of alleged sex predator
items.summary: Thirty-two years after a 10-year-old boy was tied to a tree and sexually assaulted, an audio tape of his September 1994 police interview was played for the jury Monday at the trial of his alleged attacker. Richard Neil has pleaded not guilty to 17 historical charges linked to attacks on three children.
